2006 Pennsylvania state House vote choice (Arceneaux and Kolodny 2009)

Source: R/data.R
pa2006.Rd

Survey respondents in two Pennsylvania state House districts after a field experiment in which a liberal interest group endorsed the Democratic candidate by door-to-door canvassing or by telephone (Arceneaux and Kolodny 2009). The outcome is the reported vote: abstained, Democratic candidate, Republican or other candidate, or nonresponse. Abstention is the base alternative of the published analyses and mixes routine nonvoters with occasional nonvoters, the baseline-inflated outcome of Bagozzi and Marchetti (2017, Replication I), whose Table A.3 these data reproduce. Rows are the 1,998 complete cases of that specification.

Usage

data(pa2006)

Format

A data frame with 1998 rows and 10 variables:

vote

Factor: abstain, democrat, republican_other, nonresponse.

canvass

1 if the respondent received the canvassing treatment.

phone

1 if the respondent received the telephone treatment.

democrat, republican

Party identification indicators (independents are the omitted group).

household

Number of household members.

age

Age in years.

female

1 if female.

voted2004

1 if the respondent reported voting in 2004.

district156

1 if in District 156 (open seat), 0 if in District 161.

Source

Arceneaux, K. and Kolodny, R. (2009). Educating the least informed: Group endorsements in a grassroots campaign. American Journal of Political Science, 53, 755-770. As analyzed in Bagozzi, B.E. and Marchetti, K. (2017). Distinguishing occasional abstention from routine indifference in models of vote choice. Political Science Research and Methods, 5(2), 277-294.

Provenance and terms

Taken from the replication archive of Bagozzi and Marchetti (2017), deposited at the Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/3JR2YL , version 1.1, released under CC0 1.0): the file Replication I/Least_Informed.dta (md5 0a0964fc9183e1506e893695000675a2) of PSRM Replication Files.zip, which redistributes the Arceneaux and Kolodny (2009) replication data; the rebuilding script data-raw/make_data.R of the development repository keeps the analysis variables of the published specification and the complete cases the published table uses. Original variable names: vote from votechoice_dk (1 abstain, 2 democrat, 0 republican_other, 3 nonresponse), canvass from canvass_all, phone from phone_only, democrat from sid_dem, republican from sid_rep, household from hhcount, age, female, voted2004 from vg04, district156 from d156. The published interaction terms are products of the bundled columns.

See also

Other datasets: afghan_leaders, bes1987, bes2010, cabinets, defection, fluvax, pres2004, sanctions

Examples

data(pa2006)
table(pa2006$vote)
#> 
#>          abstain         democrat republican_other      nonresponse 
#>              731              579              563              125 
f <- vote ~ canvass + phone + democrat + republican + canvass:democrat + canvass:republican +
  phone:democrat + phone:republican + household + age + female + voted2004 + district156
m0 <- mnl(f, data = pa2006)
m0$loglik                                       # published -2110.59
#> [1] -2110.593
## the published BIMNL (Table A.3) is fitted in vignette("inflation")
